claim.quote: The excavation of the caverns that will house the gigantic particle detectors of the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment in Lead, South Dakota is complete.

date.note: Date of the Fermilab press release announcing excavation completion.

name: Excavation of the DUNE far-site caverns completed at SURF
notes: Two related Fermilab announcements are cited: the 1 February 2024 completion-of-excavation press release (used for the result date) and the 15 August 2024 underground ribbon-cutting event marking the same milestone publicly; both describe the same excavation completion, not two separate results.
DUNE has published no oscillation-physics result to date, so this milestone and the ProtoDUNE-SP performance paper are the only DUNE entries in results/ (task scope note).

significance.note: A construction milestone, not a physics measurement; no significance applies.

summary.plain: Workers finished carving out the enormous underground caverns in South Dakota that will hold DUNE's giant detectors, a major step before the detectors themselves can be built.
summary.technical: Excavation of the three DUNE far-detector caverns at the 4850-foot level of SURF, announced complete by Fermilab on 1 February 2024, four years after tunnelling work began; a formal ribbon-cutting event followed on 15 August 2024.

title: Excavation of colossal caverns for Fermilab's DUNE experiment completed
why_it_matters: Completing the excavation cleared the way for detector installation to begin, the last major civil-construction milestone before DUNE's far detector modules could be assembled underground.
